title: lobivia aurea subsp. fallax
intro: Lobivia aurea subsp. fallax, commonly known as the golden crown cactus, is a species of flowering plant in the family Cactaceae, native to the Andes mountain range in South America. This cactus has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health issues, including inflammation, pain, and fever, due to its health benefits in reducing oxidative stress and improving immune function. The therapeutic actions of Lobivia aurea subsp. fallax include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, alkaloids, and glycosides. These bioactive constituents have been found to have potential therapeutic effects, including reducing inflammation and modulating the immune system.
